sources.note: Both shapes claudecode can report. system/subtype:"api_error" -> apiErrorFromSystemEvent reads error.status, retryAttempt, maxRetries, retryInMs and sets Phase=retrying when Attempt or RetryIn is present. An assistant message with isApiErrorMessage:true -> terminalAPIError sets Phase=terminal. The gate is on the boolean VALUE, never on field presence — four recorded ESC interrupts carry isApiErrorMessage:false.
The session_error rule routes a standing SessionError to StateError, and classifyAgentDone routes a hook-delivered turn_done on a FAILED turn to StateError rather than ready.

The parameterised Anthropic stub these three cells drive. --status/--error-type choose the failure, --succeed-after chooses whether it ever clears. Same streamHappyPath bytes as mock-anthropic-429 so a healthy turn is identical across mocks.

The recipe runtime block (bare_mode/env/mock) these cells use instead of a bespoke recorder. run-cell.sh refuses the cell outright if the driver does not declare DRIVE_SUPPORTS for what the recipe asks, and after the drive asserts both the driver's env receipt and that the mock actually served requests.
graceFor: error is debounced in neither direction, by decision. Its comment names provider-overloaded-retry as the recording that measures the real dwell.

The counter-evidence: two recordings on claude-code 2.1.143 whose transcripts carry six system/subtype:"api_error" lines each (retryAttempt 1..6 of 10, retryInMs 616ms..19.2s), against the same kind of loopback base-URL mock. This is what makes the 2.1.243/2.1.245 result a version regression rather than a property of the transport.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable; driver_capability: ready

## This verdict is MEASURED, and it overturns the one this cell was written with

claudecode's parser is the only one in the tree that CAN produce `ErrorPhaseRetrying` (`apiErrorFromSystemEvent`, gated on `Attempt != nil || RetryIn != nil`), and the committed 2-9 recording proves the line it reads once existed. It no longer does, which is why this trait is declared `untraced` for all eleven adapters including this one — no adapter can demonstrate a pending retry today. Four recordings driven through run-cell.sh's recipe runtime block against `tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-anthropic-error`, on claude-code 2.1.243/2.1.245:

| mock | POSTs | `system/subtype:"api_error"` lines | state arc |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--status 529 --succeed-after 1` | 2 | **0** | ready -> working -> ready |
| `--status 529 --succeed-after 3` | 4 | **0** | ready -> working -> ready |
| `--status 429 --succeed-after 3` | 5 | **0** | ready -> working -> ready |
| `--status 401 --succeed-after 0` | 22 | **0** | ready -> working -> error (at +184s) |

The ladder still runs — the 401 run's TUI pane reads `401 invalid x-api-key . Retrying in 7s . attempt 6/10`, so claude is tracking attempt and delay exactly as before — but it is now rendered to the TUI and NOT persisted. Compare the committed 2-9 recording, made on claude-code **2.1.143** against the same kind of local mock, which carries six of them:

    jq -rc 'select(.subtype=="api_error")|{status:.error.status,attempt:.retryAttempt,retryInMs}' \
      replaydata/agents/claudecode/scenarios/2-9_token-quota-exhausted/recordings/*/transcript.jsonl
    {"status":429,"attempt":1,"max":10,"retryInMs":616.45}
    ... through attempt 6, retryInMs 19183.90

Same transport (a loopback base-URL override), different CLI version. So this is `untraced` in the capability model's exact sense — the agent HAS the feature and exercising it leaves no trace in any Source the adapter reads — and `incapable` rather than `bug`, because there is no trace to mis-handle. The adapter code is correct and unchanged; the row flips back the moment claude-code persists the line again.

## What this settles for #1798

#1798 accepted a risk that a fast-recovering overload would flash red too briefly to see, and deferred the measurement to this recording. The measurement says the flash does not exist: in all three recovering runs the session never entered `error` at all, because nothing is written during the retry window. The risk that IS real is the opposite one, and the 2-24 cell measures it — a rejected credential leaves the session GREEN for 184 seconds before it turns red. A minimum hold would address neither.

## The recipe is kept, and applicable

It drives correctly and its recording is the evidence above; what it cannot do is produce a red session. Left runnable so the next reader can re-measure against a newer claude-code in one command rather than rebuilding the rig.
